pairs.subject: authorization
pairs.evidence: crates/api/src/guards.rs:42 Only an HTTP 401 increments an in-memory counter, so a scope denial is returned to the caller and is not stored as an authorization event with the operation, the missing grant, or a correlation handle.

techniques.evidence: crates/api/src/guards.rs:119 Admin and dev pass; a project key is refused. Scopes stay a separate flat set of ingest, read, and manage.
crates/api/src/main.rs:873 build_router installs access_layer::enforce as a router-wide layer. secret_eq digests both sides and compares with subtle::ConstantTimeEq.
crates/api/src/projects_keys.rs:26 An omitted scope list mints ingest and read. Unknown strings are refused at parse, and an empty list is refused.
crates/api/src/projects_keys.rs:54 Key mint is admin-only. A requested scope outside the vocabulary is a 400 at the mint; there is no public approval surface that renders the requester's list.
crates/api/src/guards.rs:144 The contract column is what the router layer reads, and this handler restates Ingest as its own literal. resolve_read_project restates Read the same way.

crates/api/src/guards.rs:42 record_failure only counts 401s. ensure_scope's 403 is not traced. ApiError::into_response writes the body and no trail line. The throttle warn names a source and a count once the budget is spent.
crates/api/src/auth.rs:29 Unset and any typo share the permissive arm. Enforced mode still distinguishes missing API key from invalid API key, and a matching expired secret returns key_expired.
crates/api/src/health.rs:107 Verdict is Up, Down, or Unknown. is_up is true only for Up, and this negation folds Unknown into not-ready. render() still prints unknown as its own word.
crates/api/src/auth.rs:147 Admin and dev reads span every project, so the owner cannot be made unaddressable. Tenancy is a TenantScope argument.
crates/api/src/auth.rs:146 scope() is the one project-key mapping. Admin project writes call ensure_can_admin before load_project, so a project key is forbidden whether or not the id exists.

crates/api/src/guards.rs:55 Auth mode is fixed at startup and build_router always registers the same routes. A missing token in dev becomes an admin-equivalent principal. check_boot will not start that posture unless the opt-out sentence is set, and warn_if_unenforced prints it.

crates/api/src/auth.rs:4 Lookup is by a stored prefix; the salt sits in the same string as the digest. A prefix miss returns before verify_key. Login responses differ for missing, invalid, and expired keys. The spoken id is api_keys.id, and list responses omit the hash.

pairs.registryProposal: failure-direction does not say whether a boot gate that refuses to start a permissive parse (unless a separate opt-out sentence is set) cures a parser that maps both an unset mode and a typo'd mode to the same permissive value.
